verdict.rationale: Google's Gemini API video docs list "character consistency" alongside image inputs and multi-turn refinement, which points toward keeping subjects consistent across generations. However, that page appears to partly describe the successor Omni model, and nothing shows how continuity carries across separate shots. Community comments add caution rather than a concrete counter-example: one questions multi-shot continuity, citing Google's own note that complex-scene consistency "remains a challenge", and one hands-on report says Whisk's video generation barely resembles the source image. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of cross-shot character or scene persistence (e.g. reference-image or shot-chaining workflow), hands-on evidence of consistent faces, backgrounds and lighting across multiple clips, and clear attribution of the consistency claim to Veo itself.
